page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s belongs to the VX1 Cloud Compute family and operates on dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 32 vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores with two threads per core running at a 2.0 GHz base frequency. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 supporting VNNI and BF16 formats, and hardware cryptographic primitives like AES and SHA-NI.

Memory provisioning stands at 128 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio typical of general-purpose systems. For primary storage, the server bundles a 1920 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, eliminating the latency overhead associated with remote networked block volumes. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not contain a discrete GPU.

Empirical benchmarks reflect strong execution across multiple domains. In memory throughput tests, large-block uncached writes achieved 194.79 GB/s, placing the server in the top tier, while uncached reads reached 295.05 GB/s. Single-threaded compression workloads exhibited leading performance, recording 40.12 GB/s in gzip and 18.04 GB/s in bzip3 decompression. Computational testing delivered a PassMark CPU score of 62267.17 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 15978.0. Operational tests demonstrated 63.95 million operations per second in Redis SET routines alongside 75.47 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s delivers solid value by bundling high-capacity local NVMe storage directly with dedicated compute cores, avoiding additional attached storage fees. While multi-core throughput in stress-ng settles in the middle tier, individual core responsiveness and memory bandwidth are notably high. This profile matches the requirements of production relational databases, distributed caching layers, application backend clusters, and continuous integration compilation systems.
description: The Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s is a general-purpose cloud instance built on dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors. It supplies 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 32 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance incorporates 128 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core, along with a bundled 1920 GB local NVMe SSD. It does not include a GPU. Benchmarks show top-tier large-block memory write bandwidth reaching 194.79 GB/s, high single-core compression rates, and strong scores across PassMark CPU tests, database operations, and Redis caching. The combination of dedicated compute resources and high local storage throughput yields balanced cost efficiency without multi-tenant contention. The vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s is well equipped for transactional relational databases, in-memory key-value stores, compression pipelines, container orchestration hosts, and heavy web serving environments.
